newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Bank Montreal, Scotiabank post strong Q1.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Bank Montreal, Scotiabank post strong Q1.

text.p: Canada's Bank of Nova Scotia and Bank of Montreal reported better than expected first-quarter earnings on Tuesday, propelling their stocks sharply higher.

Scotiabank soared C1.25 to C$52.90 on the Toronto Stock Exchange after Canada's fourth biggest bank said that its first-quarter earnings rose to C$297 million ($220 million) or C$1.14 (84 cents) a share from C$249 million ($184 million) or C95 cents (70 cents) a share in the year ago first quarter. Canadian banks' first quarter ended on Jan. 31.

Bank of Montreal was up C$1 to C$49.40 in Toronto after Canada's third biggest bank said its first-quarter earnings rose to C$322 million ($238 million) or C$1.16 (86 cents) a share from year earlier C$296 million ($219 million) or C$1.04 (77 cents) a share.
In New York, Bank of Montreal rose $1 to $36.375.
"Relative to the average forecast they were slightly better," Nesbitt Browns analyst Hugh Brown said of the banks' earnings. "But they were pretty well dead-on to our estimates."

Scotiabank had been expected to earn C$1.12 (83 cents) a share and Bank of Montreal C$1.11 (82 cents) a share in the first quarter, according to a survey of analysts' projections by the Institutional Brokers Estimate System (IBES).
The two Toronto-based banks reported strong performances from their investment banking arms.
"The securities business is very strong," said Brown. "That's the biggest single item."
International operations accounted for 52 percent of Scotiabank's earnings in the quarter and 45.1 percent at Bank of Montreal.
The two banks also reported a brighter loan loss picture.

Bank of Montreal's first-quarter provision for loan losses was unchanged at C$69 million ($52 million) from a year ago. But its problem loans fell to C$145 million ($107 million) at the end of the first quarter -- a drop of C$219 million ($162 million) from the previous quarter and C$395 million ($292 million) from a year earlier.
Scotiabank said it reduced its first-quarter loan losses to C$89 million ($66 million) from C$95 million ($70 million) a year ago.
